operational-example.copy: Use Dialog when the user must confirm, review risk, or complete a focused decision before returning to the task.

rationale: Dialog blocks the background only when the next decision changes risk, access, money, or data.
The surface, overlay, close affordance, and motion follow the ZIP overlay reference while Design System owns tokens.
Demos must close and reopen so the documentation does not show fake actions.

items.rule: Dims and blurs the task behind a required decision.
Centers the focused decision with radius, padding, border, and shadow.
Name the decision and consequence in direct language.
Signals severity or event type without replacing the title.
Expose one primary outcome, one safe secondary path, and optional close.

items: Use role dialog with aria-modal true and an accessible title.
Move focus into the dialog when it opens and restore focus to the trigger when it closes.
Escape and overlay click may dismiss only when the action is safe to cancel.
Keep primary and secondary actions reachable by keyboard.
Never use Dialog for passive feedback; use Toast or Alert Strip instead.

variants.copy: Dialog variants describe the decision job: confirmation, destructive confirmation, form, review, and success acknowledgement.

states.copy: Dialog states track lifecycle and focus: closed is unmounted, open is blocking, focus shows keyboard position, closing exits with motion, and default is ready but not shown.

demos.label: Open confirmation
demos.description: The dialog is mounted and blocks the task.

demos.label: Keyboard focus
demos.description: Focus remains visible inside the surface.

demos.label: Closing dialog
demos.description: Exit motion returns control to the trigger.

demos.label: Closed dialog
demos.description: The overlay is removed from the task.

demos.label: Default trigger
demos.description: The decision is available but not mounted.

demos.label: Success open
demos.description: The action has been reviewed and can be acknowledged.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines the decision job; state defines lifecycle and keyboard behavior. Dialog should stay scarce and intentional.

full-width.copy: Dialog uses a full-screen overlay while the decision surface keeps a readable width. Do not stretch the panel to the page.

demo.label: Closed dialog
demo.description: The user is back in the task.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Dialog remains centered on roomy viewports and becomes a near-full-width decision surface on phones while actions stack.

viewport-organization.copy: Use Dialog only when the task must pause. If the user can continue working, choose Drawer, Toast, or Inline Validation.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use a near-full-width surface and stack actions.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep the panel centered and leave overlay breathing room.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact width and clear focus restoration.

api-foundations.copy: Dialog API exposes title, description, tone, variant, lifecycle, close behavior, and actions while Design System foundations own overlay, surface, motion, voice, focus, and state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.notes: Called when local open state changes.

props.name: onAction
props.notes: Called when an action is selected.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Decision job: confirmation, destructive, form, review, or success.

props.name: state
props.notes: Lifecycle state: open, focus, closing, default, or closed.

props.name: density
props.notes: Inherited Flow density for trigger, close, actions, panel, and fields.

props.name: icon
props.notes: Optional Material Symbol override for the tone icon.

props.name: fields
props.notes: Optional short form fields rendered with Input inside the dialog body.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for decisions that block progress.
Name the consequence before the action.
Restore focus when the dialog closes.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use for passive feedback.
Do not show more than one primary action.
Do not trap users without a safe exit.

groups.title: Review
items: Check role, title, focus trap, Escape, overlay close, and reduced motion.
Confirm the action wording matches the risk.

rejectIf: Dialog is used for passive feedback.
The close or action controls do not work.
The panel stretches like a page section.
Raw color, radius, shadow, or duration values are used.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Dialog as a required decision surface: agents can propose it for risk, access, money, or destructive moments while humans confirm the consequence and exit rules.
canDecide: Use destructive tone for irreversible or high-risk changes.
Keep one primary and one safe secondary action.
mustAsk: The action can be canceled by overlay or Escape.
The decision may be handled inline or in a Drawer instead.
The content requires form fields or complex review.
rejectIf: Focus, Escape, close, or reduced-motion behavior is undefined.
miel.handoff: I am using Dialog because the process must pause for a decision. Please confirm consequence copy, close rules, primary action, and focus restoration.
